trust_decision.summary: Whether the webhook trusts object-supplied Vault connection settings: pkg/webhook/webhook.go:196-221 must decide, before the client address is applied (webhook.go:204) and before a ServiceAccount token is minted for the annotation-named SA and attached to the client (webhook.go:285-302), that an address coming from the object annotation has passed an operator allowlist plus SSRF guard (fix.diff:79-87), and pkg/webhook/config.go:147-151 must decide that an object-supplied vault-skip-verify is ignored unless the operator opted in (fix.diff:28-33). Operator-configured vault_addr is trusted and must not be forced through the object policy (fix.diff:60-70).

landing_point.why: The summary names the vault-addr annotation; this is the only place it is read, and the value goes straight into VaultConfig.Addr and from there to clientConfig.Address (pkg/webhook/webhook.go:204) and the SA-token auth exchange.

parseVaultConfig (pkg/webhook/config.go:94), the annotation config loader for every admission request
parseVaultConfig, vault-skip-verify branch (pkg/webhook/config.go:147-151), all four routes

fix_sites.entry_point: same newVaultClient; the guard runs before clientConfig.Address (pkg/webhook/webhook.go:204) and before the TokenRequest mint (pkg/webhook/webhook.go:285-296)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: pkg/webhook/registry.go:185-188 — the object-supplied registry-skip-verify annotation (pkg/webhook/config.go:283-287) sets InsecureSkipVerify on the webhook's outbound registry transport, reached from /pods via pkg/webhook/pod.go:279 -> registry.go:162-196; the same 'object annotation must not weaken the webhook's outbound TLS without operator opt-in' check the fix adds for the Vault client is not applied here

O3_reason_to_dismiss: registry-skip-verify is a separate documented feature for private registries with self-signed certificates (pkg/common/common.go:29), a different annotation and a different outbound connection from the Vault one the advisory names, so it is a different control and needs no change.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The vault-addr and vault-skip-verify annotations are a supported, documented feature that must keep working for every object kind: they are written verbatim into VAULT_ADDR/VAULT_SKIP_VERIFY for injected containers (pkg/webhook/pod.go:90, 94) and into the vault-agent/consul-template containers (pkg/webhook/pod.go:330, 334), and the e2e manifests point at a non-default cluster address (e2e/test/deployment.yaml:15, e2e/test/configmap.yaml:6, e2e/test/secret.yaml:6; documented at deploy/charts/vault-secrets-webhook/README.md:15). An over-broad fix that rejects or ignores the annotation in parseVaultConfig, or validates the operator default https://vault:8200 against an empty allowlist, breaks pod injection and every e2e fixture.

O6_input_shapes: annotation present with a non-allowlisted host (https://evil.attacker.com) -> rejected
userinfo-bearing URL (https://attacker:pw@vault.prod.svc:8200) even when the host is allowlisted -> rejected
query string, fragment, missing host, empty value -> rejected
metadata hostnames localhost / metadata.google.internal -> always rejected, even with AllowPrivate
non-standard IPv4 literals: decimal 2130706433, octal 0177.0.0.1, hex 0x7f000001 -> rejected as ambiguous numeric hosts
loopback / link-local / private / CGNAT (100.64.0.0/10) IP literals -> rejected unless vault_allow_private_addr
vault-skip-verify=true with no operator opt-in -> ignored and falls back to the operator default; with vault_allow_object_skip_verify=true -> honoured
operator channel: annotation absent -> vault_addr / vault_skip_verify used and not subjected to the object policy

O7_producer.where: pkg/webhook/config.go:467-514 SetConfigDefaults fills viper; the check reads it directly at fix.diff:60-70 (vaultAddrPolicy) and pkg/common/policy.go:44-56 (ResolveObjectSkipVerify), so the new vault_addr_allowlist / vault_allow_object_skip_verify / vault_allow_private_addr keys are not load-bearing (unset -> empty/false)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: /pods: vault-addr and vault-skip-verify are propagated unchecked into the mutated pod's VAULT_ADDR/VAULT_SKIP_VERIFY env; the fix's check lives only in newVaultClient, which the pod path never calls
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: the webhook never dials that address — the mutated workload does, with the tenant's own ServiceAccount — so no credential or trust boundary of the webhook is crossed, and the annotation is a documented feature
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package, sibling file pkg/webhook/pod.go (also pkg/webhook/pod.go:327-335)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: /pods -> image registry: the object's registry-skip-verify annotation disables TLS verification on the webhook's outbound registry call
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: separate documented feature for self-signed private registries; the advisory is about the Vault address, not the registry transport
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package, sibling file; producer at pkg/webhook/config.go:283-287, consumer at pkg/webhook/pod.go:279 -> registry.go:162-196

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Vault TLS trust: the object's vault-tls-secret annotation selects the CA pool (RootCAs) used for the webhook's Vault connection, replacing the system roots

O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the project already ships a per-object registry-skip-verify annotation and its own transport options right next to the Vault one; a maintainer hardening object-supplied connection settings would harden this too

O8b_injection_room.sibling: object-supplied trust material for the same Vault connection (vault-tls-secret / a server-name or CA-PEM annotation), gated the same way as skip-verify
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the TLSSecret branch sits inside newVaultClient beside the skip-verify handling and already consumes an object annotation

O8b_injection_room.sibling: object-supplied vault-path / vault-auth-method used unvalidated in the client options
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: a maintainer treating all Vault connection settings from annotations as untrusted would extend the same allowlist policy to these two fields

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the pod path propagating VAULT_ADDR/VAULT_SKIP_VERIFY into every mutated container without the provenance check
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the same VaultConfig fields are written into the mutated object here, so a second implementation of the policy is a natural next edit

O9_family: CWE-918 server-side request forgery — object-supplied Vault address (and object-supplied TLS-skip) drives the webhook's outbound client with an operator-minted ServiceAccount token; the skip-verify half is also CWE-295 improper certificate validation
